title: Free-generator and relation comparison under ring and module sheafification
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], small in the universe of the sheaves and presheaves below, and let $\varphi:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ be a morphism of presheaves of commutative rings. Write $\eta_M:M\to M^\#$ for sheafification [def-weil-pbc-sheafification], using the underlying abelian sheafification and the extended $\mathcal B^\#$ action for module presheaves [lem-pc-sites-module-sheafification-interface]. For a presheaf of sets $T$, put $\mathcal B[T](U)=\bigoplus_{t\in T(U)}\mathcal B(U)[t]$ [def-weil-pbc-free-module], with $b[t]|_V=b|_V[t|_V]$. For a sheaf of rings $R$ and a sheaf of sets $S$, write $R[S]$ for the module sheafification [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification] of $U\mapsto R(U)[S(U)]$, with generator map $i:S\to|R[S]|$; here $|-|$ denotes the underlying sheaf of sets. The maps $|\mathcal A|\to|\mathcal A^\#|$, $|\mathcal B|\to|\mathcal B^\#|$, and $\mathcal B\times\mathcal B\to|\mathcal B^\#|\times|\mathcal B^\#|$ are sheafifications of set presheaves. For every set presheaf $T$ there is a canonical isomorphism of module sheaves
$$c_T:\mathcal B[T]^\#\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal B^\#[T^\#],\qquad c_T(\eta_{\mathcal B[T]}([t]))=i(\eta_T(t)).$$
Equivalently, for every $\mathcal B^\#$-module sheaf $N$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], restriction to generators and the sheafification unit gives a natural bijection
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal B^\#}(\mathcal B[T]^\#,N)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C)}(T^\#,|N|).$$
Put $F=\mathcal B[\mathcal B]$ and $E=\mathcal B[\mathcal B\times\mathcal B]\oplus\mathcal B[\mathcal B\times\mathcal B]\oplus\mathcal B[\mathcal A]$. Let $r:E\to F$ be the linear relation map with the three generator formulas $[(a,b)]\mapsto[a+b]-[a]-[b]$, $[(f,g)]\mapsto[fg]-g[f]-f[g]$, and $[h]\mapsto[\varphi(h)]$. There are generator-normalized isomorphisms
$$c_F:F^\#\cong\bar F=\mathcal B^\#[\mathcal B^\#],\qquad c_E:E^\#\cong\bar E=\mathcal B^\#[\mathcal B^\#\times\mathcal B^\#]\oplus\mathcal B^\#[\mathcal B^\#\times\mathcal B^\#]\oplus\mathcal B^\#[\mathcal A^\#].$$
They satisfy $c_F\circ r^\#=\bar r\circ c_E$, where $\bar r$ is the sheaf-module map given by the same three formulas on all local sections of the sheafified rings, with $\varphi$ replaced by $\varphi^\#$. In particular, equality on the original presheaf generators determines these sheafified module maps uniquely.

proof.text: By [lem-pe-ring-sheafification-underlying-sets], $|\eta_{\mathcal A}|$ and $|\eta_{\mathcal B}|$ exhibit set sheafifications, with their unit identifications. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-sheafification-sets-exact] to $|\mathcal B|\times|\mathcal B|$: the projection-normalized comparison identifies its set sheafification with $|\mathcal B^\#|\times|\mathcal B^\#|$, and its unit is $\eta_{\mathcal B}\times\eta_{\mathcal B}$. Thus all three set-sheafification assertions in the statement hold. The site and values lie in the common universe required by both cited statements. Ring sheafification is a ring morphism, so $\eta_{\mathcal B}(a+b)=\eta_{\mathcal B}(a)+\eta_{\mathcal B}(b)$, $\eta_{\mathcal B}(fg)=\eta_{\mathcal B}(f)\eta_{\mathcal B}(g)$, and $\varphi^\#\eta_{\mathcal A}=\eta_{\mathcal B}\varphi$.

proof.text: For a $\mathcal B^\#$-module sheaf $N$, restrict its scalars along $\eta_{\mathcal B}$. A map of set presheaves $a:T\to|N|$ extends uniquely to a $\mathcal B$-linear presheaf map $\mathcal B[T]\to N$ by $\sum b_t[t]\mapsto\sum\eta_{\mathcal B}(b_t)a(t)$. Uniqueness is coefficientwise linearity and the basis expansion of [def-weil-pbc-free-module]. This extension commutes with restrictions: along $V\to U$, both orders give $\sum\eta_{\mathcal B}(b_t|_V)a_V(t|_V)$, since $a$ is natural and restrictions of $N$ are semilinear. Consequently restriction to generators gives a natural bijection $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal B}(\mathcal B[T],N)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{PSh}}(T,|N|)$.

proof.text:
Apply [lem-pc-sites-module-sheafification-interface] to $\mathcal B[T]$ and [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] to $T$. Together with step 2 this gives
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal B^\#}(\mathcal B[T]^\#,N)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal B}(\mathcal B[T],N)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{PSh}}(T,|N|)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{Sh}}(T^\#,|N|).$$
The map $t\mapsto\eta_{\mathcal B[T]}([t])$ extends uniquely to $k_T:T^\#\to|\mathcal B[T]^\#|$. The displayed bijection sends $h$ to $|h|k_T$: this follows by precomposing with $\eta_T$ and the two uniqueness properties. Apply the last assertion of [lem-trf-free-module-sheaf-universal-property], with ring $\mathcal B^\#$, generator sheaf $T^\#$ and representing pair $(\mathcal B[T]^\#,k_T)$. It supplies the unique isomorphism $c_T$ with $|c_T|k_T=i$, hence the required generator formula. Naturality follows by restriction to $t$: composition with any generator map or target module morphism has the same image through the displayed bijections. In particular maps out of $\mathcal B[T]^\#$ are equal whenever they agree on every $\eta_{\mathcal B[T]}([t])$.

proof.text: Apply step 3 with $T=|\mathcal B|$ and the set-unit identification of step 1 to obtain $c_F$. For the three terms of $E$, use $T_1=T_2=|\mathcal B|\times|\mathcal B|$, $T_3=|\mathcal A|$ and write $P_j=\mathcal B[T_j]$. There is a canonical $d:(\bigoplus_{j=1}^3P_j)^\#\cong\bigoplus_{j=1}^3P_j^\#$: extend the presheaf map $(x_j)\mapsto(\eta_{P_j}x_j)$ by the module-sheafification universal property. Its inverse is $b((y_j))=\sum_j\iota_j^\#(y_j)$, where $\iota_j:P_j\to\bigoplus_jP_j$ are the inclusions. The identity $bd=1$ follows after precomposition with the unit, and $db=1$ follows on each summand after its unit; these tests are justified by [lem-pc-sites-module-sheafification-interface]. Finite sums of module sheaves here are sectionwise finite products, with coordinatewise gluing and operations. Compose $d$ with the three isomorphisms of step 3, and then the set-unit identifications of step 1 on their generator sheaves, to obtain $c_E$. This proves its asserted normalization on each of the three original generator families.

proof.text:
Use [lem-trf-free-module-sheaf-universal-property] to define the three components of $\bar r$ by their stated generator formulas, now on all sections of $\mathcal B^\#\times\mathcal B^\#$ and $\mathcal A^\#$. Each formula is a morphism of set sheaves, since the ring operations, module operations, generator maps, and $\varphi^\#$ commute with restriction. The universal property extends each uniquely to a linear sheaf map; summing on the three summands gives $\bar r$. On an original generator of each family, both $c_F r^\#$ and $\bar r c_E$ have respectively the following values, writing $i$ for the generator of $\bar F$:
$$i(\eta_{\mathcal B}(a)+\eta_{\mathcal B}(b))-i(\eta_{\mathcal B}(a))-i(\eta_{\mathcal B}(b)),$$
$$i(\eta_{\mathcal B}(f)\eta_{\mathcal B}(g))-\eta_{\mathcal B}(g)i(\eta_{\mathcal B}(f))-\eta_{\mathcal B}(f)i(\eta_{\mathcal B}(g)),$$
$$i(\varphi^\#(\eta_{\mathcal A}(h))).$$
For the first route these equalities use step 1 and the module-unit identity $\eta_P(bx)=\eta_{\mathcal B}(b)\eta_P(x)$ supplied by [lem-pc-sites-module-sheafification-interface]; for the second they are the definitions of $\bar r$ and $c_E$. Step 3's uniqueness applies on each $P_j^\#$ and step 4's direct-sum comparison then gives $c_F r^\#=\bar r c_E$. The same tests prove the final uniqueness assertion for maps from $F^\#$ and $E^\#$: precompose with the sheafification units and use sectionwise linearity on the original bases.
